# StepanovWeil — the square-root bound for the residue character of any pattern

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** cited from a published paper; not proved in Lean · **Diagram:** [One wheel at a time: squares, characters and the number 24](../../GRAPH.md#one-wheel-at-a-time-squares-characters-and-the-number-24)

On an odd prime wheel, take an offset pattern whose members sit on different positions of the wheel and multiply a position's distances from all of them. The quadratic character of that product, added around the wheel, has square at most (the number of offsets minus 1) squared times the wheel size: a sum of wheel-size many terms of size 1 cancels down to about the square root of the wheel size. This is Weil's bound (1948) for the curve y² = the product; Stepanov (1969) found an elementary proof with an auxiliary polynomial that vanishes to high order. Cited, not proved in Lean; Stepanov's method is the route to a Lean proof, since it needs no algebraic geometry.

Published work this node rests on or relates to; each entry says how.

- [S. Kopparty, The Weil bounds, Topics in Finite Fields (Rutgers, 2013)](https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~sk1233/courses/finitefields-F13/weil.pdf) — states the bound and proves special cases by Stepanov's method
- [Finite Fields: Root Sets, Frobenius, and Algebraic Structure, §18.23 (arXiv:2610.36727)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36727) — Weil bounds for polynomial character sums by Stepanov's method; a possible blueprint for a Lean proof

## Claims

<a id="weil_pattern_bound"></a>
### `weil_pattern_bound`

On an odd prime wheel, for a pattern of at least one offset with no two on the same position, the squared character sum of the product of distances is at most (pattern size − 1)² times the wheel size (cited).

```lean
/-- **Weil's bound, pattern form** (cited). On an odd prime wheel, for an offset
pattern with at least one member and no two members on the same position, the
square of the character sum of the product of distances is at most (pattern
size − 1)² times the wheel size. -/
def weil_pattern_bound : Prop :=
  ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime], p ≠ 2 → ∀ T : Finset ℕ, 0 < T.card → w T p = T.card →
    (∑ x : ZMod p, quadraticChar (ZMod p) (∏ t ∈ T, (x + (t : ZMod p)))) ^ 2 ≤
      ((T.card : ℤ) - 1) ^ 2 * p
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Justification:** cited — A. Weil, Sur les courbes algébriques et les variétés qui s'en déduisent (1948); elementary proof by S. A. Stepanov (1969), in the form of W. M. Schmidt, Equations over Finite Fields (1976), the bound on the character sum of a polynomial with distinct roots, by the degree minus 1 times the square root of the field size. Not proved in Lean.
